name: Stack from Chill Dog
description: Defending Chill Dog opens the high-leg enclosure before advancing through guard. Forward pressure must not fold the partner onto the neck or wrench the shoulder.
summary: Defending Chill Dog requires a safe base and release of the high-leg enclosure before advancing through the remaining guard.
overview:
The top player faces a bottom guard player using Chill Dog; the head, shoulder or arm may still be enclosed. Forward pressure must not fold the partner onto the neck. The reviewed sources do not establish stacking as a required Chill Dog escape or an automatic Half Guard result.

Keep the free hand available for framing while preventing the isolated elbow from being pulled further away from your torso. The opponent changing the hand around your head signals the move beyond New York, not a turtle escape. Keep a balanced base and early inside frames; tap instead of moving against a completed choke or joint lock.

Move through available space with a stable base. Stop and release any trapped neck, shoulder or knee before changing direction; do not force a roll or stack to preserve the route.

Instructional sources: [Brandon McCaghren — Gogoplata from rubber guard](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wn39-wrfsbs); [Eddie Bravo — Chill Dog / Invisible Collar clarification](https://www.10thplanetjj.com/forum/threads/17657-Chill-Dog-Invisible-Collar-Question).

flashcards.question: Stack from Chill Dog (top): What must be controlled before seeking leg slack?
flashcards.answer: Use balanced supports and an inside free arm while keeping the isolated elbow compact before attempting upper-body release.
flashcards.answer_line: Your base and inside frame beside the trapped arm

plausible: Only your free-hand grip on their raised ankle
A wide free-hand post with the captured elbow flared
trap: Your knee base while both forearms remain outside

flashcards.question: Stack from Chill Dog (top): What does their cleared head-side arm mean for you?
flashcards.answer: The neck-cleared hand position and knee hug can still hold the arm and posture; do not mistake a grip change for release.
flashcards.answer_line: Your upper body may still be enclosed by Chill Dog

plausible: The captured elbow has followed their hand inside the knee
The high shin has dropped below your shoulder line
trap: The knee hug opened when their controlling arm moved

flashcards.question: Stack from Chill Dog (top): What should replace pressure that folds them onto the neck?
flashcards.answer: Reduce the forward load and recover balanced space; neck-folding pressure does not substitute for releasing the enclosure.
flashcards.answer_line: Unload and seek an opening in the high-leg connection

plausible: More forward drive with a wider knee base
Lifting their hips higher before extracting the arm
trap: Keep the hips elevated while pulling your head back

flashcards.question: Stack from Chill Dog (top): Where should you create slack to free the upper body?
flashcards.answer: Open space in the high-leg connection while keeping the head and captured arm aligned.
flashcards.answer_line: At the hip and thigh without turning the caught head

plausible: At the toes while the thigh stays clamped
Only between your own knees on the floor
trap: At the free shin while the controlling thigh still clamps

flashcards.question: Stack from Chill Dog (top): When should the shoulder be pulled out?
flashcards.answer: Retrieve shoulder and elbow only after sufficient slack exists, rather than trying to pull a fixed joint through pressure.
flashcards.answer_line: Once the high enclosure opens around the arm

plausible: While their knee hug still pins the elbow
As soon as their hips lift off the mat
trap: Once the head clears while the knee hug still fixes the arm

flashcards.question: Stack from Chill Dog (top): What is the first useful passing checkpoint?
flashcards.answer: Upper-body clearance and inside arm position prepare later passing. They do not by themselves clear the remaining knees.
flashcards.answer_line: A free shoulder with the elbow recovered inside

plausible: Their hips elevated while your arm stays trapped
Your chin raised while the high leg stays tight
trap: A free hand with the elbow still outside their thigh

flashcards.question: Stack from Chill Dog (top): What establishes a half-guard result, if one remains?
flashcards.answer: The destination depends on the resulting leg configuration; the named stack does not guarantee half guard.
flashcards.answer_line: One of your legs actually caught between theirs

plausible: Your head clearing the high leg alone
Their hand changing around your neck
trap: Both of their knees between your hips after the high leg drops

defender.name: Stack from Chill Dog Defender
defender.description: Stack from Chill Dog (defender): Keep the opposing hand on the mat and hug the knee before changing the head-side grip. Bring the knee toward the chest through hip movement so the neck-clearing motion does not twist the knee.
defender.overview:
The top player faces a bottom guard player using Chill Dog; the head, shoulder or arm may still be enclosed. Forward pressure must not fold the partner onto the neck. The reviewed sources do not establish stacking as a required Chill Dog escape or an automatic Half Guard result.

Keep the opposing hand on the mat and hug the knee before changing the head-side grip. Bring the knee toward the chest through hip movement so the neck-clearing motion does not twist the knee. Move the controlling arm around the head while keeping the leg and trapped arm connected.

Use the forearm near the shoulder line to manage forward pressure; do not let the frame collapse across your own wrist. Keep the knee hug while choosing further control such as Invisible Collar or an omoplata setup. Return the legs to a comfortable guard if the opponent withdraws the elbow or stacks your upper back.

Move through available space with a stable base. Stop and release any trapped neck, shoulder or knee before changing direction; do not force a roll or stack to preserve the route.

When the high connection must open, use a supported hip escape and a knee returning inside for guard retention. A forearm at the shoulder blocks a crossface and incoming chest pressure while you make that space.
key_principles: Secure New York first: Keep the opposing hand on the mat and hug the knee before changing the head-side grip.
Turn onto the hip: Bring the knee toward the chest through hip movement so the neck-clearing motion does not twist the knee.
Clear the neck: Move the controlling arm around the head while keeping the leg and trapped arm connected.
Place the inside frame: Use the forearm near the shoulder line to manage forward pressure; do not let the frame collapse across your own wrist.
Maintain the arm trap: Keep the knee hug while choosing further control such as Invisible Collar or an omoplata setup.
Recover when control opens: Return the legs to a comfortable guard if the opponent withdraws the elbow or stacks your upper back.

flashcards.question: Stack from Chill Dog (bottom): What connection retains the arm while pressure is mild?
flashcards.answer: When the position remains comfortable, keep the arm isolated with the knee supported; do not retain it through harmful stacking.
flashcards.answer_line: The overhook with a supported knee hug

plausible: A loose foot grip with the knee drifting away
Both hands behind the head with the arm uncovered
trap: A high knee with the overhook opened for a head grip

flashcards.question: Stack from Chill Dog (bottom): How should you adjust the high leg through available space?
flashcards.answer: A hip-angle change supports the raised knee without pulling the foot against a fixed joint.
flashcards.answer_line: Turn the hip to bring the knee toward the torso

plausible: Hold the hip flat and pull the ankle harder
Push the knee away while the foot remains caught
trap: Lift the foot first while leaving the knee behind the shoulder

flashcards.question: Stack from Chill Dog (bottom): When the stack becomes neck-loading, what should you do?
flashcards.answer: Release the unsustainable high connection and obtain an unloaded reset rather than trying to preserve Chill Dog at the neck's expense.
flashcards.answer_line: Open the high control and stop the neck load

plausible: Keep the leg high until the passer gives up
Tighten the arm wrap and pull the head closer
trap: Lower only the free leg while keeping the high grip taut

flashcards.question: Stack from Chill Dog (bottom): Where should the early forearm barrier sit?
flashcards.answer: An inside forearm manages forward shoulder pressure while there is still space; it should not collapse across your wrist.
flashcards.answer_line: Inside at the approaching shoulder line

plausible: Outside the shoulder with the wrist folded inward
Along their outer upper arm with the elbow away
trap: At the collarbone with the forearm collapsed onto your wrist

flashcards.question: Stack from Chill Dog (bottom): After releasing the stack, what rebuilds guard?
flashcards.answer: Once the high connection and harmful load are gone, move the hips behind an inside shoulder frame and recover knee space.
flashcards.answer_line: A hip escape that returns a knee behind the frame

plausible: Another high foot reach before any knee space
Both arms chasing the opponent's head
trap: A hip slide while both knees remain beyond their hips
